title: a frozen, implemented ACED scenario specifies an edge that cannot fire
note: registry.feature:75 'a squad missing its governances block is rejected' freezes the same unreachable behavior that init-quill's step 3 states in prose: the skill constructs the only payload it ever writes and that payload always carries a governances block, so the validation cannot be reached from inside its own workflow. line 62's governances-block rejection has no reachable trigger. Two exits: delete the rule, or make it reachable by having step 3 validate the FOUND entry — a quill entry already in squads[] shape whose squad lacks governances should be treated as an older shape and rewritten to canonical rather than classified up-to-date and left alone. The second is the useful form: it is the only path by which a hand-edited or partially-migrated registry ever gets repaired. Either way the registry node's spec and suite need a matching amendment; as authored they specify only what the skill can currently do.

title: the forward face does not scale with diff size, and the bar should say so
note: Both remediation producers independently reasoned that a narrow diff licenses a narrow pre-flight — one loaded zero governances, the other two of seven. The cold judge ruled there is no scoped-remediation exemption: whether a one-scenario edit raises a scope or structural question is the bars' OUTPUT, not their precondition, so a producer cannot know the oracle bar is quiet without reading it. Two independent instances in one round is doctrine-shaped, not two lapses. Sharpest evidence: the spec-writer node's own README argues that a producer which never read the oracle bar has no reason to reach the scope-finding node — and its producer then skipped that bar while editing that graph.
